scope: Stable source-code vulnerability shapes. These records are navigation and proof checklists, not signatures or CVE claims.

signals: ownership or tenant predicate is absent
rules.trace: Trace the external identifier through canonicalization and lookup to the final authorization decision.
counterevidence: query scoped by subject or tenant

signals: privileged action has multiple entry points
one path bypasses the shared policy
background or bulk path calls service directly
rules.trace: Enumerate every caller of the privileged operation and compare enforcement before the shared side effect.
Follow every exceptional and default branch to the effective allow or deny result.

signals: client supplies price, credit, role, entitlement, or status
rules.trace: Compare the client value with the server-side source of truth at the commit point.
Build the allowed state machine and trace a skipped, reordered, or replayed transition to its postcondition.
counterevidence: single-use transition token bound to state

signals: refund, invite, reset, coupon, or approval can be retried
rules.trace: Trace success, retry, rollback, and exception paths around the one-time asset.
counterevidence: idempotency record covers the side effect

signals: multiple workers or requests can enter
rules.trace: Write an explicit two-actor interleaving and map each step to transaction and lock boundaries.
counterevidence: exclusive lock spans check and write

rules.trace: Trace duplicate delivery through deduplication scope, side effect, commit, and acknowledgement.

signals: filesystem or authorization check before later use
rules.trace: Identify the mutable object between check and use and whether the same handle or identity is preserved.

signals: untrusted value concatenated into query text
rules.trace: Track value and grammar position into the executed query, including wrappers and query builders.

signals: user value reaches executable or arguments
rules.trace: Distinguish direct argv execution from shell parsing and trace each controllable grammar boundary.

signals: template or expression compiled from input
rules.trace: Identify the sink grammar and prove whether the final encoder or sandbox matches that exact context.
counterevidence: correct context encoder at final sink
strict sandbox with unreachable dangerous objects

signals: normalization before or after policy differs
rules.trace: Follow decoding, normalization, symlink resolution, containment, open, and later rename or extraction.
counterevidence: storage key not interpreted as a path

rules.trace: Trace each entry name and link through normalization to the final extraction root and overwrite policy.

signals: unsafe YAML or native object stream
rules.trace: Bind attacker influence to parser mode, allowed types or resolvers, instantiated behavior, and reachable side effects.
counterevidence: external entities and network resolvers disabled

signals: policy validates text before client parsing
multiple URL parsers or normalization stages
rules.trace: Trace raw input through decoding, parsing, validation, canonicalization, and connector destination.
Follow redirect policy and header propagation across every hop and scheme change.
counterevidence: sensitive headers stripped on origin change

rules.trace: Compare the address authorized by policy with the address actually connected by the effective transport.

signals: token header selects algorithm or key
rules.trace: Map attacker-controlled token fields to verifier configuration and every accepted identity claim.
counterevidence: trusted key selection independent of token URL fields

signals: session survives login, logout, password change, or role change
rules.trace: Trace session minting, binding, rotation, lookup, invalidation, and authorization cache lifetime.

signals: token not bound to subject or purpose
rules.trace: Trace entropy, storage, binding, comparison, expiry, consumption, and related state changes.
Derive the effective middleware and route order for the production entry point.
counterevidence: all entry points share protected composition

signals: example config can enter release build
rules.trace: Resolve defaults, configuration precedence, build mode, and deployment files to the reachable effective value.

signals: trusted proxy headers affect origin or identity
CORS or CSRF setting is broad
rules.trace: Trace the setting through proxy topology and framework defaults to the security decision it controls.

signals: private package name can resolve publicly
rules.trace: Derive package identity, registry precedence, namespace ownership, and lock provenance.

signals: CI action, image, or dependency uses mutable tag
rules.trace: Trace the mutable reference to the privileged build step and resulting artifact provenance.
counterevidence: untrusted step has no release capability

signals: install hook, plugin, generator, or build script executes
input comes from fork or untrusted branch
rules.trace: Map untrusted build input to code execution and the credentials, filesystem, or publication capability exposed.
